title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 6 questions (6.1)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A new team member asks what identity governance and administration (IGA) means. Which description is BEST?
choices: Policy-based control of identities and access, from provisioning to reviews
Vaulting and rotating the passwords of shared privileged accounts
Signing users in to many applications through one central login page with MFA
Collecting security logs and alerting on suspicious network events
questions.answer: Policy-based control of identities and access, from provisioning to reviews
questions.explanation: IGA combines identity lifecycle administration with governance such as certifications, policies and reporting. Central sign-on is access management, and vaulting is PAM.

questions.stem: A company already uses an SSO and MFA product, but auditors want proof of who has access to what and periodic reviews of that access. Which capability fills the gap?
choices: Access management
Identity governance and administration
Security information and event management
Privileged access management
questions.answer: Identity governance and administration
questions.explanation: Visibility of access across systems and periodic reviews are IGA functions. The existing SSO and MFA tool controls sign-in, not entitlement governance.

questions.stem: Automating account creation for new hires, access changes for transfers and removal for leavers belongs to which part of IGA?
choices: Access certification
Federation
Identity lifecycle management
Separation of duties
questions.answer: Identity lifecycle management
questions.explanation: Joiner, mover and leaver processes are lifecycle management, driven in ISC by authoritative sources, identity profiles and lifecycle states. Certification reviews access already granted.

questions.stem: An employee moved from Finance to Sales but still holds Finance entitlements months later. Which IGA control MOST directly prevents this?
choices: Encrypting the Finance application's database
Longer passwords for users who change departments
A single sign-on portal for the Sales applications
Role access driven by the department attribute
questions.answer: Role access driven by the department attribute
questions.explanation: Attribute-based role membership and lifecycle changes adjust access when the department changes, preventing privilege creep. Passwords and encryption do not remove entitlements.

questions.stem: Why does an IGA design name the HR system as an authoritative source?
choices: It is the only system where SailPoint can provision accounts
It is the trusted record that creates identities and their attributes
It removes the need to correlate any accounts that come from other sources
It stores the passwords that users enter at sign-in
questions.answer: It is the trusted record that creates identities and their attributes
questions.explanation: An authoritative source drives identity creation and attributes such as department and manager, which govern access. Other sources' accounts still need correlation.

questions.stem: Business users request access through hundreds of individual entitlements and often pick the wrong ones. Which IGA practice helps MOST?
choices: Letting every user request any entitlement without approval
Hiding the access request page until a certification ends
Removing all entitlements and granting access only by ticket
Grouping entitlements into access profiles and roles
questions.answer: Grouping entitlements into access profiles and roles
questions.explanation: Access modeling bundles entitlements into access profiles and roles that users and approvers understand. It reduces errors without removing governance.

questions.stem: An auditor asks which identities hold a specific payroll entitlement across all accounts. Which IGA capability answers this MOST directly?
choices: Reading the payroll application's sign-in logs for the past several weeks
Reviewing the firewall rules in front of the payroll server
Searching correlated accounts and entitlements for that entitlement
Asking each manager to report access for their team
questions.answer: Searching correlated accounts and entitlements for that entitlement
questions.explanation: IGA aggregates accounts and entitlements and correlates them to identities, so search shows who holds the entitlement. Sign-in logs show only who used the app recently.

questions.stem: In identity security, what does compliance mean?
choices: Meeting, and proving you meet, regulations, standards and policies
Encrypting every system that stores personal information
Passing a single annual penetration test of the network
Making sure every single user signs in with multi-factor authentication
questions.answer: Meeting, and proving you meet, regulations, standards and policies
questions.explanation: Compliance means following the required rules and showing evidence of it, for example with certification records and audit trails. Encryption and MFA are controls, not compliance itself.

questions.stem: A financial company must show that access to its general ledger is reviewed every quarter. Which ISC feature produces this evidence?
choices: A transform that standardizes ledger account names
A VA cluster dedicated to the ledger source
An access certification campaign whose reviewer decisions are recorded
A lifecycle state that disables inactive ledger accounts
questions.answer: An access certification campaign whose reviewer decisions are recorded
questions.explanation: Certifications have reviewers approve or revoke access and keep the decisions as audit evidence. Lifecycle states and transforms do not prove periodic review.

questions.stem: The same user can create a vendor and approve payments to that vendor. Which control addresses this risk?
choices: A federation trust with the payment provider
A longer password for the user's finance account
A delta aggregation of the finance source
A separation of duties policy
questions.answer: A separation of duties policy
questions.explanation: SoD policies flag or prevent combinations of access that allow one person to commit and hide fraud. Passwords and aggregation do not detect toxic combinations.

questions.stem: An auditor asks for evidence that a user's access to a sensitive application was approved before it was granted. Which record is MOST useful?
choices: The identity profile's attribute mappings
The access request and its approval history
The application's current list of entitlements
The user's last sign-in time on the application
questions.answer: The access request and its approval history
questions.explanation: Access request records show who requested, who approved and when, which is the evidence of prior approval. An entitlement list shows what exists, not who approved it.

questions.stem: Aggregation finds application accounts that do not correlate to any identity. Why is this a compliance concern?
choices: No one is accountable for them, so they may be orphaned or misused
They cause the identity profile to stop refreshing
They slow down every certification campaign for the source
They prevent the source from being used in access requests
questions.answer: No one is accountable for them, so they may be orphaned or misused
questions.explanation: Uncorrelated accounts may belong to leavers or unknown owners, a classic audit finding. Governance requires correlating them or removing them.

questions.stem: Checking for an SoD conflict when access is requested, before approval, is what kind of control?
choices: Preventive
Detective
Compensating
Corrective
questions.answer: Preventive
questions.explanation: Stopping or flagging a violation before access is granted is preventive. A certification or policy scan that finds existing violations is detective.

questions.stem: A US healthcare provider must protect patient health information and control who can access it. Which regulation applies MOST directly?
choices: FERPA
HIPAA
SOX
PCI DSS
questions.answer: HIPAA
questions.explanation: HIPAA governs US protected health information. SOX covers financial reporting, PCI DSS card data and FERPA student records.

questions.stem: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
choices: Authentication applies to applications; authorization applies to devices
Authentication grants access rights; authorization checks the password
Authentication verifies who the user is; authorization decides what the user may access
Authentication happens after authorization, once access is known
questions.answer: Authentication verifies who the user is; authorization decides what the user may access
questions.explanation: Authentication proves identity and authorization then decides which resources and actions are allowed. Authorization relies on a known, authenticated identity.

questions.stem: A user signs in successfully to a web application but receives an access denied error when opening the payroll page. Which process denied the request?
choices: Aggregation
Federation
Authentication
Authorization
questions.answer: Authorization
questions.explanation: The sign-in worked, so authentication succeeded; the denial is the application deciding the user lacks permission. That decision is authorization.

questions.stem: A help desk analyst can sign in to Identity Security Cloud but does not see the Admin options other engineers see. What MOST likely explains this?
choices: The analyst signed in through a federated identity provider
The analyst's identity is in an inactive lifecycle state
The analyst's user level does not grant those admin rights
The analyst's password does not meet complexity rules
questions.answer: The analyst's user level does not grant those admin rights
questions.explanation: User levels such as Admin, Source Admin or Helpdesk decide what each user may do in ISC, which is authorization. A password problem would stop sign-in altogether.

questions.stem: In what order are authentication and authorization normally performed for a request?
choices: Authorization first, then authentication if the access is granted
Only authorization, for users already in a directory
Both at once, as a single combined step
Authentication first, then authorization of the requested action
questions.answer: Authentication first, then authorization of the requested action
questions.explanation: A system must first know who is asking before it can decide what that identity may do. Authorization without authentication would not know whose rights to check.

questions.stem: A developer says OAuth 2.0 alone tells the application who the user is. What is the BEST correction?
choices: OAuth 2.0 authenticates users by sending their password to the application
OAuth 2.0 authorizes access; OpenID Connect adds authentication on top
OAuth 2.0 and SAML are the same protocol with different token formats
OAuth 2.0 is for authentication; OpenID Connect handles only authorization
questions.answer: OAuth 2.0 authorizes access; OpenID Connect adds authentication on top
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 issues access tokens to authorize API access, and OpenID Connect adds the ID token that authenticates the user. OAuth never sends the password to the client app.

questions.stem: A script calls the ISC API using an OAuth client created with limited scopes. Which statement about the call is correct?
choices: Its credentials authenticate the client, and its scopes limit what it may call
The client must also send an admin's password to be authorized
The scopes authenticate the client, and its secret alone limits what it may call
The token is valid for any API, because scopes are informational only
questions.answer: Its credentials authenticate the client, and its scopes limit what it may call
questions.explanation: The client ID and secret prove the client's identity to get a token, and scopes and rights then limit what it may do. Scopes are enforced, not informational.

questions.stem: An entitlement such as a group membership in an application is an example of which kind of information?
choices: Authentication data that proves who the account is
Compliance data that records a reviewer's decision
Federation data that links two identity providers
Authorization data that defines what an account may do
questions.answer: Authorization data that defines what an account may do
questions.explanation: Entitlements grant permissions inside a system, so they are authorization data. IGA governs who holds them.

questions.stem: Which BEST describes identity federation?
choices: Granting every user the same entitlements in all systems
Copying every user's password into each of the connected applications nightly
A trust that lets one domain's identity provider vouch for users to others
Merging several directories into one physical database
questions.answer: A trust that lets one domain's identity provider vouch for users to others
questions.explanation: Federation lets a service provider trust authentication done by an external identity provider, so users need no separate credentials. No passwords are copied.

questions.stem: A company configures its employees to sign in to Identity Security Cloud through Microsoft Entra ID using SAML. Which roles do the two systems play?
choices: Entra ID is the service provider and ISC is the directory
Entra ID is the identity provider and ISC is the service provider
ISC is the identity provider and Entra ID is the service provider
Both systems act as identity providers for each other
questions.answer: Entra ID is the identity provider and ISC is the service provider
questions.explanation: The system that authenticates the user and issues the assertion is the identity provider; the application relying on it, here ISC, is the service provider.

questions.stem: In SAML 2.0 single sign-on, what does the identity provider send to the service provider after the user authenticates?
choices: A digitally signed XML assertion about the user
A copy of the user's directory record and group list file
A Kerberos ticket granting ticket for the service provider
The user's password encrypted with the service provider's key
questions.answer: A digitally signed XML assertion about the user
questions.explanation: The IdP sends a signed SAML assertion naming the user and possibly attributes, and the SP validates the signature. Passwords never reach the SP.

questions.stem: An engineer is setting up a new SAML trust between an identity provider and a service provider. What must the two sides exchange?
choices: Metadata, including endpoints and the signing certificate
A shared database account for user lookups
The identity provider's private signing key
Each user's password hash so the SP can verify sign-ins offline
questions.answer: Metadata, including endpoints and the signing certificate
questions.explanation: Federation partners exchange metadata, including the public signing certificate the SP uses to verify assertions. Private keys and password hashes never leave the IdP.

questions.stem: An application team using OpenID Connect asks which token tells the application who signed in. What is the answer?
choices: The SAML assertion, wrapped inside an OAuth grant
The ID token, a signed JWT about the authentication
The access token, which carries the user's password
The refresh token, which carries the user's profile
questions.answer: The ID token, a signed JWT about the authentication
questions.explanation: In OIDC the ID token is a signed JWT with claims about the user and the sign-in event. Access tokens authorize API calls and refresh tokens get new tokens.

questions.stem: A user opens the service provider's URL and is redirected to the identity provider to sign in before returning. What is this flow called?
choices: Identity provider-initiated single sign-on
Just-in-time provisioning
Service provider-initiated single sign-on
Pass-through authentication
questions.answer: Service provider-initiated single sign-on
questions.explanation: When the user starts at the application and is sent to the IdP, the flow is SP-initiated. IdP-initiated starts at the identity provider's portal.

questions.stem: What is a main security benefit of federating sign-in to many applications through one identity provider?
choices: Users no longer need to authenticate at all after onboarding
Applications can skip authorization checks entirely for all federated users
Each application keeps its own password store as a backup
Authentication and MFA are enforced in one place, with no app passwords
questions.answer: Authentication and MFA are enforced in one place, with no app passwords
questions.explanation: Federation centralizes authentication policy and removes per-application passwords. Applications still authorize what each user may do.

questions.stem: An employee uses a smart card with a PIN to sign in. Which authentication factor category does the card itself belong to?
choices: Something you have
Something you are
Somewhere you are
Something you know
questions.answer: Something you have
questions.explanation: A physical smart card is a possession factor; the PIN is a knowledge factor, together making MFA.

questions.stem: A policy requires multi-factor authentication. Which combination satisfies it?
choices: A password plus a security question answer
A password plus a second, different password
A PIN plus a memorized passphrase
A password plus a code from an authenticator app
questions.answer: A password plus a code from an authenticator app
questions.explanation: MFA needs factors from different categories, such as knowledge plus possession. Two knowledge factors are still single-factor.

questions.stem: Users want to sign in to Identity Security Cloud with their existing Active Directory credentials without a separate federation product. Which option provides this?
choices: SAML federation with the tenant as the identity provider
A lookup transform on the user's AD account name
Pass-through authentication to the AD source through a VA
A personal access token issued from each user's AD account
questions.answer: Pass-through authentication to the AD source through a VA
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication sends the credentials to the AD source's VA cluster to check against Active Directory. A personal access token is for API access, not interactive sign-in.

questions.stem: The security team wants an MFA method that resists phishing because it is bound to the real website's origin. Which method is BEST?
choices: Emailed one-time passcodes
FIDO2/WebAuthn security keys or passkeys
One-time passcodes sent by SMS to a registered phone
Security questions
questions.answer: FIDO2/WebAuthn security keys or passkeys
questions.explanation: FIDO2/WebAuthn binds the cryptographic response to the site's origin, so a fake site cannot replay it. SMS and email codes can be phished and relayed.

questions.stem: An authenticator app shows a six-digit code that changes every 30 seconds, computed from a shared secret and the current time. What is this method?
choices: Push notification approval
Certificate-based authentication
Time-based one-time password (TOTP)
Kerberos ticket
questions.answer: Time-based one-time password (TOTP)
questions.explanation: TOTP derives short-lived codes from a shared secret and the clock, which is why device time must be accurate. Push methods ask the user to approve a prompt instead.

questions.stem: A laptop unlocks with a fingerprint reader. Which factor category is used?
choices: Something you do
Something you know
Something you have
Something you are
questions.answer: Something you are
questions.explanation: Fingerprints are biometric, an inherence factor. The laptop is a device, but the fingerprint itself is what is checked.

questions.stem: Domain-joined Windows users reach internal web apps without typing a password again, using tickets from a domain controller. Which protocol is this?
choices: SAML 2.0
Kerberos
RADIUS
SCIM
questions.answer: Kerberos
questions.explanation: Kerberos issues tickets from the domain controller's key distribution center for integrated Windows sign-on. SCIM is a provisioning protocol, not authentication.

questions.stem: Match each identity security term to its meaning.

pairs.match: Verifying that users are who they claim to be
Deciding which resources and actions a user may use
Trusting another domain's identity provider to sign users in
Policy-based control and review of who has access to what
Following regulations and policies and proving it with evidence

targets_extra: Encrypting data while it is stored on disk
questions.explanation: These core terms are tested together. Encryption at rest is a data protection control, not one of these concepts.

questions.stem: Users already sign in with a password. Which TWO additions would each make the sign-in multi-factor?
choices: A fingerprint scan
A security question answer
A memorized PIN
A second password
A FIDO2 security key
questions.explanation: A security key (possession) or a fingerprint (inherence) adds a different category to the password (knowledge). Security questions, PINs and second passwords are all knowledge factors, so they do not make it multi-factor.

questions.stem: Put the steps of a service provider-initiated SAML sign-in in order.
items: The user opens the service provider's URL
The service provider redirects the browser to the identity provider with an authentication request
The identity provider authenticates the user, including MFA if required
The identity provider posts a signed assertion back to the service provider
The service provider validates the assertion and starts a session
questions.explanation: SP-initiated SSO starts at the app, goes to the IdP for authentication and returns with a signed assertion that the SP validates.
